youtube.title: Why Is Jesus Called Immanuel?
youtube.line1: Why is Jesus called Immanuel? In the Bible, a frightened king told God no. God answered anyway, with a sign (Isaiah 7:14).
youtube.line2: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." (Isaiah 7:14, KJV)
youtube.read_it: Read it yourself: Isaiah 7:1-14; 2 Kings 16:5-8; Matthew 1:18-25; Matthew 28:20; 1 Corinthians 15:3-4.
youtube.insight_line: The Immanuel sign was first given to King Ahaz, who refused God's offer and, in that same war, begged the king of Assyria "save me" (2 Kings 16:7). God gave the sign anyway, and the child it pointed to was named JESUS, "for he shall save".

next_teaser: More Old Testament promises that came true in Jesus, one at a time.
shareable_fact: The Immanuel promise of Isaiah 7:14 was first spoken to King Ahaz, who had just refused God's offer of any sign; in that same war he begged the king of Assyria to save him (2 Kings 16:7).
ask_line: Follow for Old Testament promises that came true in Jesus, one at a time.
pinned_comment: The Immanuel promise was first given to King Ahaz, a frightened son of David who refused God's offer of a sign (Isaiah 7:10-14). In that same war he begged the king of Assyria to save him (2 Kings 16:7). About 700 years later another son of David, Joseph, heard "fear not" and obeyed (Matthew 1:20-24). Which son of David are you more like when you are afraid? Read it: Isaiah 7:1-14; 2 Kings 16:5-8; Matthew 1:18-25; Matthew 28:20; 1 Corinthians 15:3-4.
